rv.q: And yet, in Allan’s script and in director Nick Bowling’s staging, Whitaker and Baxter’s story often seems to take a backseat to competing interests.
CAMPAIGNS, INC is brilliantly written (Will Allan), masterfully directed (Nick Bowling), and splendidly acted by the entire cast.
TimeLine company member Will Allan has written a highly entertaining, fast-paced comedy, based upon the actual 1934. California gubernatorial race...
In this author's opinion, director Nick Bowling could not have gathered a finer cast to bring this story to life. From the ensemble to the leads, not a note is out of place.
But as a comic guidebook to how propaganda works, and how even the best candidate on paper can be demolished in three dimensions, it’s a peach.
It's a spot-on, if somewhat on-the-nose historical tale of a lesser-known but prophetic event.
Although the story is interesting, the execution has some issues.
It’s difficult to find this take funny since we know where endless fabrication without consequences and aggressive political gaslighting ends.
The production is filled with history and political views and is a solid history lesson, so you are getting educated and entertained in one fell swoop.

cn.t: Critics praise this world premiere for its timely exploration of political manipulation's origins, with strong performances and sharp writing illuminating how fake news tactics emerged in 1934 California.
